title: Lecture 1 — Instructor Tutorial
subject: Programming Languages
description: 29 questions and answers transcribed from the instructor tutorial shared on Blackboard. Source wording and marked answers are preserved; the source key for question 22 needs clarification.

questions.question: Why is it useful for a programmer to have some background in language design, even though they may never design a programming language?
options: It allows them to bypass the need for an operating system.
It eliminates the need to compile high-level source code.
It helps them understand the significance of implementation and learn new languages more easily.
It completely replaces the study of algorithm analysis and data structures.
questions.correctAnswer: It helps them understand the significance of implementation and learn new languages more easily.
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects C: It helps them understand the significance of implementation and learn new languages more easily.

questions.question: How can knowledge of programming language characteristics benefit the computing community as a whole?
options: It ensures that only one universal programming language will ever be developed.
It helps informed decision-makers choose better languages that can eventually displace poorer ones.
It guarantees hardware prices will drop steadily each year.
It eliminates the need for software maintenance across all applications.
questions.correctAnswer: It helps informed decision-makers choose better languages that can eventually displace poorer ones.
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: It helps informed decision-makers choose better languages that can eventually displace poorer ones.

questions.question: Which programming language has dominated scientific computing over the past 60 years?
options: Fortran
COBOL
Lisp
Prolog
questions.correctAnswer: Fortran
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects A: Fortran

questions.question: Which programming language has dominated business applications over the past 60 years?
options: ALGOL 60
COBOL
Smalltalk
APL
questions.correctAnswer: COBOL
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: COBOL

questions.question: Which programming language dominated artificial intelligence applications developed prior to 1990?
options: Ada
C
Lisp
Visual Basic
questions.correctAnswer: Lisp
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects C: Lisp

questions.question: In what programming language is most of the UNIX operating system written?
options: Fortran
C
Java
Perl
questions.correctAnswer: C
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: C

questions.question: What is a primary disadvantage of having too many basic features in a programming language?
options: Code readability is impaired because different programmers often learn and use different feature subsets.
Programs will automatically fail to link with standard system libraries.
The language becomes unusable on modern von Neumann machines.
Pure interpreters become completely impossible to implement.
questions.correctAnswer: Code readability is impaired because different programmers often learn and use different feature subsets.
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects A: Code readability is impaired because different programmers often learn and use different feature subsets.

questions.question: How can user-defined operator overloading harm the readability of a program?
options: It causes the source file to take up more physical disk space.
It converts compiled code back into machine instructions automatically.
It can lead to confusion if operators are given unusual meanings that conflict with common conventions.
It prevents variables from being defined inside subroutines.
questions.correctAnswer: It can lead to confusion if operators are given unusual meanings that conflict with common conventions.
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects C: It can lead to confusion if operators are given unusual meanings that conflict with common conventions.

questions.question: Which of the following illustrates a lack of orthogonality in the design of C?
options: Variables can hold both positive and negative integers.
Structs can be returned from functions, but arrays cannot.
Subprograms can take zero or more parameters.
Loops can be created using both while and for statements.
questions.correctAnswer: Structs can be returned from functions, but arrays cannot.
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: Structs can be returned from functions, but arrays cannot.

questions.question: Which programming language used orthogonality as a primary design criterion?
options: ALGOL 68
Fortran
Java
questions.correctAnswer: ALGOL 68
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects A: ALGOL 68

questions.question: What primitive control statement was historically used to build more complicated control structures in languages that lacked them?
options: switch
goto
try-catch
yield
questions.correctAnswer: goto
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: goto

questions.question: What does it mean for a program to be reliable?
options: It executes using the least possible amount of main memory.
It performs according to its specifications under all conditions.
It has been translated purely through a Just-in-Time compiler.
It can be executed on non-von Neumann computer architectures without modification.
questions.correctAnswer: It performs according to its specifications under all conditions.
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: It performs according to its specifications under all conditions.

questions.question: Why is type checking the parameters of a subprogram important?
options: It automatically speeds up macro expansion in preprocessors.
It ensures that variable bit representations match what the receiving subprogram expects, avoiding subtle errors.
It prevents the computer from requiring a program counter.
It converts all formal parameters to pointers at compile time.
questions.correctAnswer: It ensures that variable bit representations match what the receiving subprogram expects, avoiding subtle errors.
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: It ensures that variable bit representations match what the receiving subprogram expects, avoiding subtle errors.

questions.question: What is aliasing?
options: Using two or more distinct names in a program to access the same memory cell.
Assigning multiple types to a variable simultaneously at runtime.
Defining functions that accept varying numbers of arguments.
The automatic optimization of machine code by a compiler.
questions.correctAnswer: Using two or more distinct names in a program to access the same memory cell.
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects A: Using two or more distinct names in a program to access the same memory cell.

questions.question: What is exception handling?
options: An instruction set feature that increases the physical memory bus width.
The ability of a program to intercept runtime errors, take corrective measures, and continue.
The process of replacing symbolic assembly with intermediate bytecode.
A mechanism that prohibits functions from using recursion.
questions.correctAnswer: The ability of a program to intercept runtime errors, take corrective measures, and continue.
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: The ability of a program to intercept runtime errors, take corrective measures, and continue.

questions.question: Why is readability important to writability?
options: Because programmers spend time reading documentation rather than writing code.
Because writing code requires programmers to frequently reread parts of the code already written.
Because modern compilers cannot optimize programs that are hard to read.
Because pure interpreters require comments in order to parse statements.
questions.correctAnswer: Because writing code requires programmers to frequently reread parts of the code already written.
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: Because writing code requires programmers to frequently reread parts of the code already written.

questions.question: How is the cost of compilers for a given language related to the design of that language?
options: Simpler, more orthogonal languages typically require less effort and cost to implement compilers for than complex languages.
Languages that enforce strong typing do not require any compiler design costs.
Interpreted languages always cost more to compile than compiled languages.
The number of comments allowed in a language determines the hardware costs of the compiler.
questions.correctAnswer: Simpler, more orthogonal languages typically require less effort and cost to implement compilers for than complex languages.
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects A: Simpler, more orthogonal languages typically require less effort and cost to implement compilers for than complex languages.

questions.question: What have been the two strongest influences on programming language design over the past 60 years?
options: Cloud infrastructure and database normalization
Computer architecture and software design methodologies
Hardware peripherals and network protocols
Artificial neural networks and graphics processors
questions.correctAnswer: Computer architecture and software design methodologies
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: Computer architecture and software design methodologies

questions.question: What is the name of the category of programming languages whose structure is dictated by the von Neumann computer architecture?
options: Functional languages
Logic languages
Rule-based languages
Imperative languages
questions.correctAnswer: Imperative languages
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects D: Imperative languages

questions.question: What two programming language deficiencies were identified as a result of research into software development in the 1970s?
options: Incompleteness of type checking and inadequacy of control statements
Lack of markup integration and excess of dynamic arrays
Too much functional recursion and excessive operator overloading
Absence of bytecode engines and poor disk access speeds
questions.correctAnswer: Incompleteness of type checking and inadequacy of control statements
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects A: Incompleteness of type checking and inadequacy of control statements

questions.question: What are the three fundamental features of an object-oriented programming language?
options: Recursion, pointers, and memory stacks
Data abstraction, inheritance, and dynamic method binding
Feature multiplicity, orthogonality, and aliasing
Compilation, pure interpretation, and preprocessor directives
questions.correctAnswer: Data abstraction, inheritance, and dynamic method binding
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: Data abstraction, inheritance, and dynamic method binding

questions.question: Which language was the first to support the fundamental features of object-oriented programming?
options: Smalltalk
SIMULA 67
Java
questions.correctAnswer: Smalltalk
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects A: Smalltalk This is the supplied key’s answer. The wording is worth checking with the instructor: SIMULA 67 predates Smalltalk and is commonly credited as the first object-oriented language.

questions.question: Which of the following represents a conflict between two language design criteria?
options: Expressivity versus symbol availability
Software reliability versus execution cost (e.g., array index bound checking)
Lexical parsing versus syntax analysis
Static typing versus symbol table lookups
questions.correctAnswer: Software reliability versus execution cost (e.g., array index bound checking)
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: Software reliability versus execution cost (e.g., array index bound checking)

questions.question: What are the three general methods of implementing a programming language?
options: Assembly, microprogramming, and macroprogramming
Scripting, markup, and database mapping
Compilation, pure interpretation, and hybrid implementation systems
Static linking, dynamic linking, and loading
questions.correctAnswer: Compilation, pure interpretation, and hybrid implementation systems
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects C: Compilation, pure interpretation, and hybrid implementation systems

questions.question: Which produces faster program execution, a compiler or a pure interpreter?
options: A pure interpreter
A compiler
Both produce identical execution speeds
Neither; only preprocessors produce machine instructions
questions.correctAnswer: A compiler
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: A compiler

questions.question: What primary role does the symbol table play during the compilation process?
options: It serves as a database storing type and attribute information of user-defined names.
It converts intermediate code directly into assembly language comments.
It tracks execution speed during runtime to optimize CPU registers.
It contains pre-written machine instructions for external hardware devices.
questions.correctAnswer: It serves as a database storing type and attribute information of user-defined names.
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects A: It serves as a database storing type and attribute information of user-defined names.

questions.question: What is the role of a linker?
options: It parses raw source code characters into lexical units.
It connects a user program to system programs and library code to produce an executable image.
It performs runtime array bound checks on memory cells.
It expands macro definitions like #define and #include.
questions.correctAnswer: It connects a user program to system programs and library code to produce an executable image.
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: It connects a user program to system programs and library code to produce an executable image.

questions.question: Why is the von Neumann bottleneck important?
options: It causes syntax errors when high-level programs use too many loops.
The connection speed between memory and CPU is the primary limiting factor in computer speed.
It prevents hybrid systems from using Just-in-Time compilation.
It forces all programming languages to be dynamically typed.
questions.correctAnswer: The connection speed between memory and CPU is the primary limiting factor in computer speed.
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: The connection speed between memory and CPU is the primary limiting factor in computer speed.

questions.question: What is an advantage of implementing a language using a pure interpreter?
options: Programs execute 10 to 100 times faster than compiled systems.
Source-level debugging and runtime error reporting are easy to implement.
Code takes significantly less space in memory during runtime.
There is no need for a symbol table or lexical analysis.
questions.correctAnswer: Source-level debugging and runtime error reporting are easy to implement.
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: Source-level debugging and runtime error reporting are easy to implement.
